author.name: Scout - VRChat Head of Quality Assurance

comments.value: An additional feature I'd like to see with this would be the choice between how to handle multiple senders inside the box. One option could average the positions out between all senders, and another could be based on order of entry (first, last, etc). As well as a simple bool/float for whether or not something is inside of the object, or perhaps an INT counting how many senders are inside. These could all be very useful.
very yes, one could create bounding boxes for game mechanics in avatars with this
would just love a Box Contact. you have to place contact in weird way to get them to do what you want, or move them up and down fast to make it fill the part i want to trigger a thing
This would be extra useful now that contacts are in worlds; things like dance floors or paint canvases could be handled this way.

Box shaped contact senders and receivers are on the way! They are currently testable in the beta SDK `3.10.4-beta.2`. They include an option for calculating proximity as the distance to a face of the box, as an alternative to the suggestion made here.

We mentioned box contacts briefly in our most recent developer update: https://ask.vrchat.com/t/developer-update-21-may-2026/48458#p-89491-box-shaped-contacts-9
@{65f4b1a3d0a7a0c657a7d3a8|full_name} any news on if box physbone colliders will be added eventually too?

details: Having a Contact Receiver type that is an an adjustable box shape where X, Y, Z positions of a contact sender within the bounds are output as 3 float parameters would be incredibly useful for any number of avatar interactions, including far easier touch-screens using less contacts, musical instruments, Radars, etc. I've included a Mock-up of what this mode could look like.
title: 3-Axis Box Contact Receiver
